text:
In the world of product management, clarity is your best ally. This week, I stumbled upon a headline about a government hiring an industrial policy chief without requiring any understanding of industrial policy. It struck me how often organizations overlook the fundamentals when making critical hiring decisions. 

As we dive deeper into AI and data-driven products, we need leaders who not only understand the technology but also grasp the nuances of human behavior and market dynamics. This intersection is where structured product management meets coaching—a blend that can drive real outcomes.

Remember, decisions rooted in understanding create impact. So, as you build your teams and make hiring choices, ask yourself: Are we prioritizing the right skills that will propel our vision forward? Reflect on your own experiences—what's one misstep you've learned from in hiring that you wish you could redo?

diagram_spec.diagram_prompt: A comparison diagram illustrating the differences between hiring for technical skills versus hiring for a blend of technical and human behavior skills in product management.
